claims.excerpt: De POA-refunddienst werd na twaalf weken publiek gelanceerd.
claims.claim: The POA refund service launched to the public after a twelve-week delivery period.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: We passed alpha and beta Service Standard assessments and launched to the public in only 12 weeks.
claims.narrative: Het POA-refundteam lanceerde de dienst na twaalf weken
claims.explanation: The source says the service launched in twelve weeks; the excerpt preserves that duration and public-launch milestone.
claims.materiality: The launch timing is central to the account.

claims.excerpt: Een oplevering binnen de aanvankelijk gevraagde paar weken werd niet haalbaar geacht als de gebruikersdienst kwalitatief moest blijven.
claims.claim: The team initially was asked to deliver within a couple of weeks, and judged that timeline infeasible if it was to deliver a quality service.
claims.label: F1 minor immaterial imprecision
claims.evidence: We were initially asked to deliver the service in a matter of weeks, which put huge pressure on everyone and we quickly discovered would not be possible if we wanted to create a quality service for our users.
claims.narrative: de aanvankelijk gevraagde termijn van enkele weken niet haalbaar werd geacht met behoud van een kwalitatieve gebruikersdienst
claims.explanation: The infeasibility conditional on maintaining quality is supported, but “paar weken” is more specific than the source’s unspecific “a matter of weeks” and the narrative’s “enkele weken.”
claims.materiality: The narrower duration slightly sharpens the deadline but does not change the main point that the requested short timeline was infeasible.

claims.excerpt: De aanpak begon bij de ervaring van aanvragers: die werd eerst naar alpha gebracht.
claims.claim: The team began with the applicant experience and took it to alpha first.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: My team focused on the users applying for refunds first and this is what we took to the alpha assessment.
claims.explanation: The source explicitly says the team focused on refund applicants first and took that work to alpha.
claims.materiality: This is a central sequencing choice in the piece.

claims.excerpt: Het werk voor caseworkers kwam later.
claims.claim: Work for caseworkers came later than the work focused on refund applicants.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence: Plans for the caseworker user came later.
claims.explanation: The source and narrative both state that caseworker plans came later.
claims.materiality: This is a central sequencing choice in the piece.

claims.excerpt: Tijdens de private beta wisselden tweewekelijkse sprints af tussen aanvragen aannemen en tijd vrijmaken voor testen, onderzoek en verwerking.
claims.claim: During private beta, fortnightly sprints alternated between accepting applications and setting aside time for testing, research, and processing.
claims.label: F1 minor immaterial imprecision
claims.evidence: We achieved this by splitting our fortnightly sprints in two: testing, researching and accepting applications in the first week and then suspending submissions to concentrate on testing, researching and processing applications the second.
claims.narrative: Tijdens de private beta wisselden tweewekelijkse sprints af tussen aanvragen aannemen en tijd besteden aan testen, onderzoek en verwerking.
claims.explanation: The broad pattern is supported, but the source specifies two distinct weeks: the first combined intake with testing and research; the second suspended submissions and focused on testing, research, and processing. The excerpt compresses that arrangement and does not state when intake was suspended.
claims.materiality: The omitted week-by-week detail slightly reduces precision about how intake and processing fit into the sprint rhythm.

claims.excerpt: Zo combineerde het POA-refundteam een duidelijke volgorde — eerst aanvragers, daarna caseworkers — met gereserveerde tijd voor onderzoek en testen tijdens de beta.
claims.claim: The team’s approach combined an applicant-first, caseworker-later sequence with time reserved for research and testing during beta.
claims.label: F0 faithful
claims.evidence:
My team focused on the users applying for refunds first and this is what we took to the alpha assessment. Plans for the caseworker user came later.

We achieved this by splitting our fortnightly sprints in two: testing, researching and accepting applications in the first week and then suspending submissions to concentrate on testing, researching and processing applications the second.
claims.narrative: De beschreven aanpak combineerde een volgorde waarin aanvragers eerst kwamen met expliciet gereserveerde tijd voor onderzoek en testen.
claims.explanation: This is a supported synthesis of the stated user-group sequence and the research and testing time built into private-beta sprints. It does not claim that these practices caused the launch or results.
claims.materiality: It captures the piece’s central account of the team’s working approach.
